canonical_question: Does the 'partial RX' mentioned at >700 °C refer to partial dynamic recrystallization or static recovery?

question_variants.question: Does the 'partial RX' mentioned at >700 °C refer to partial dynamic recrystallization or static recovery?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text attributes the yield strength drop to 'partial RX' and work softening but does not explicitly define whether RX refers to dynamic or static recrystallization/recovery in this context.

answers.answer: The text suspects yield strength drop and work softening occur due to partial RX at high temperatures but does not specify if this is dynamic recrystallization or static recovery.
answers.measurement_outcome: Suspected partial RX causing yield strength drop and work softening
answers.boundary_limitation: Nature of RX (dynamic vs static) not explicitly defined
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.
